about: Accessories for the museum (feature #39). Concise original summaries; every story paragraph cites its source and the date it was read. Facts are limited to what the cited sources state; a year or spec a source doesn't give is left out.

items.name: Visoflex reflex housing
items.line: Turns a rangefinder into a reflex camera · ground-glass focusing

facts.label: What it is
facts.value: Mirror box, ground glass and viewfinder

story.text: A reflex housing made by Leitz to add ground-glass focusing to its rangefinder cameras, updating the PLOOT housing of the 1930s. It fits between camera and lens, so long lenses and close-ups can be focused through the lens.
The Visoflex I first served screw-mount Leicas and was then made for the M bayonet after the M3 arrived. The Visoflex II was made for both mounts; the Visoflex III for M cameras only.

items.name: SBOOI 50 mm bright-line finder
items.line: An optical finder for screw-mount Leicas · 50 mm frame

story.text: An optical viewfinder Leica made for its screw-mount rangefinders, showing a bright frame for the 50 mm lens. The first version is engraved "5 cm"; a later one "50mm", with grooves on the sides for grip.

items.name: Leicavit
items.line: A trigger winder in the base plate · up to two frames a second

facts.label: What it is
facts.value: Rapid winder in place of the base plate

facts.label: Fits (Leicavit M)
facts.value: M-A, MP, M6, M6 TTL, M7, M4-P, M4-2

story.text: Introduced alongside the original Leica MP, the Leicavit advances the film and re-cocks the shutter in one pull of a trigger under the camera, without taking the camera from the eye.
story.source: Red Dot Forum, "Leica Reintroduces the Leicavit M"

story.text: The first production ended in 1966. Leica revived it in 2003 and made it until December 2020, then brought it back in 2025 as a regular product in three finishes.
story.source: Red Dot Forum, "Leica Reintroduces the Leicavit M"

items.name: Leicameter MR
items.line: A clip-on light meter that couples to the shutter dial

facts.label: What it is
facts.value: Shoe-mounted light meter for M cameras

facts.label: Fits
facts.value: M1, M2, M3 and the M4 models

story.text: A light meter that sits in the accessory shoe and turns with the shutter-speed dial, so setting the speed on one sets it on the other: the feel of a built-in meter on cameras that had none.

items.name: Leica Motor M
items.line: A battery motor drive for film M bodies · 1.5 or 3 frames a second

facts.label: Fits
facts.value: MP, M7, M6 TTL, M6, M4-2, M4-P

story.text: A motor that fits under a film M body and winds on after every frame, at one and a half or three frames a second. It has its own tripod thread.

items.name: Visoflex (Typ 020)
items.line: An electronic viewfinder for digital M bodies

story.text: The Visoflex name returned for the digital age: an electronic viewfinder that clips onto a digital M and shows exactly what the lens sees, the job the mirror housing once did.
